title: Minimum Initial Energy to Finish Tasks
summary: Given an array tasks where each element is [actuali, minimumi], actuali is the energy spent on the i^th task, and minimumi is the minimum energy required to start the i^th task.
statement: Given an array tasks where each element is [actuali, minimumi], actuali is the energy spent on the i^th task, and minimumi is the minimum energy required to start the i^th task. You can complete the tasks in any order. The goal is to determine the least initial energy needed to complete all tasks.
constraints: Choose any order and return the least starting energy that permits every task.
hints: A task’s minimum-minus-cost margin measures how costly it is to postpone.
Process larger margins first and track total energy already spent.
Sort by minimum-actual descending; required is max(required,spent+minimum), then add actual to spent.
Swapping an inverted adjacent pair never increases the required start, establishing the sorted order by exchange argument.
editorial: Swapping an inverted adjacent pair never increases the required start, establishing the sorted order by exchange argument.
